$comment: Machine-readable inventory of this directory's conformance corpus, referenced normatively by spec.md Sec 8.5. Not itself a fixture: it sits at the top level of tests/, outside every category directory, so a runner that only walks category directories never encounters it. schema_version names the shape of THIS file; a runner MUST reject a manifest whose schema_version it does not implement rather than guess at an unrecognized shape. 'categories' is the CLOSED set of category directory names a conforming versions/0.7/tests/ MUST contain -- exactly these names, no more, no fewer -- with the exact number of fixtures each one MUST contain today. A 'fixture' is one <name> stem shared by that category's sibling files: one .ktav/.json/.canonical.ktav triple under valid/, one .ktav/.json pair under invalid/ or parseable-unrepresentable/, or one .json file under unrepresentable/. These counts are intentionally exact, not merely 'non-empty': a runner pointed at a stale or truncated corpus (e.g. an old spec version's tests/ directory, or a working copy where fixtures failed to check out) still has every category present and non-empty, and only an exact count catches that it is running fewer cases than the corpus actually defines. Growing the corpus MUST include updating the relevant category's count in this file, in the same change that adds the fixture; this is deliberate friction, matching the discipline scripts/validate_corpus.py's --corpus-inventory-lock already applies to the corpus's raw bytes. 'fixture_flags' lists individual fixtures that need handling other than 'decode this file as UTF-8 text'; today the only defined flag is 'raw_bytes', which marks a fixture whose primary .ktav input is deliberately not valid UTF-8 (Sec 6.15) and MUST be read as a raw byte sequence and handed to the implementation under test unchanged -- a runner MUST NOT read such a fixture through a text-decoding API whose behavior on invalid encoding is to substitute or drop the offending bytes (e.g. .NET's File.ReadAllText, or a non-fatal TextDecoder) before the parser under test ever sees them, since that silently replaces the exact condition Sec 6.15 requires the parser to detect. Every fixture not listed here, in every category, is ordinary UTF-8 text with no special handling.

fixture_flags.note: Sec 6.15 InvalidUtf8: the .ktav input is deliberately not valid UTF-8; read it as raw bytes, not as decoded text.
